questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university was situated not too far from the center of London with great transportation possibilities and Queen Mary University of London is a part of the Russell Group which is a prestigious group of universities in the UK including Oxford and Cambridge.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yes, they have a great newsletter

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Yes, it was easy to get in touch

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Dansk KFUK is a great place to live and it is easy to make young Danish friends there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: KFUK is about an hour away from Queen Mary with the tube. Take the Metropolitan line and then the Hammersmith & City line! It is much better than taking the Jubilee and then the Central.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There is a pre-registration and then an enrollment once you arrive. You can find the requirements for English language proficiency here:
https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/accepted-english-language-tests-and-qualifications/

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always write to the Global Opportunities office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: They cancelled one of my classes on the day I was supposed to have it but I found managed to get another class instead

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
First you pre-register but then for approx. two weeks from you have your first event at Queen Mary, you can add and drop your classes as they also may clash. Your schedule is ready about a week before starting the courses. You can find the courses here:
https://www.qmul.ac.uk/modules/

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Varying levels of the courses but I would recommend taking a level 6 course as it usually is of higher quality.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same but the lectures and seminars are only 1 hour and the seminars only have about 20 people in them instead of 48.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Globalisation: Issues & Debates, The UK & the EU, British Politics, Comparative Politics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them all except Comparative Politics. British Politics wasn't on a very high level but it was a great introduction to the British way. The professeur in Globalisation: Issues & Debates and the seminar tutor I had was really great at teaching (and even without slides :0)

questions.answer: ETA for the UK and the public transportation. Get a student Oyster (you can do it online) and get a travel card on it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are over 300 different student clubs. Find them at the student fair or at
https://www.qmsu.org/clubs-socs/find/

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The debate club was super nice

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the UK. Brighton is only 1,5 hours away and 15 pounds for a round tour. Get a railcard so you get 30% of your journeys. The trains are super expensive.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy - London is a very international city

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the student societies

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everyone has their own culture

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The scones

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Participate in the intro-week 2. Get a student oyster card 3. get started on your essays early

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying a different school system with easy access to the professeurs and with many different student societies that included all students from different study fields.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The British are super young when they start so they were shocked that I was 24.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
